topic: Diffusion Models for 3D Shape and Scene Generation: Methods, Representations, and Evaluation

per_sentence.text: Denoising diffusion models have emerged as a prominent framework because, unlike generative adversarial networks (GANs), variational autoencoders (VAEs), and normalizing flows, they explicitly model the data distribution, enabling them to faithfully generate outputs that reflect content diversity (Li et al., 2026).

per_sentence.text: Prior work has explored diverse strategies, including learning distributions over gradient fields that model shape surfaces, as in ShapeGF, and training GANs over latent variables that encode shapes, exemplified by IM-GAN which models shapes as neural fields, and l-GAN, while r-GAN generates point clouds directly (Li et al., 2026).
